open_experiments.summary: roll-plan.ts's buildRollChild mutates the CALLER's in-memory rollBook (splice parent, push child) during PLAN-BUILDING, before syncSwingManagement's immediately-following runRoll (the actual closeAndRollSwingPosition DB write) confirms success. If that write later fails for this row (child insert throws, grade race), the parent stays OPEN in the DB but rollBook already reflects the swap for the REST of this same batch pass -- a later row's budget/cap gate could be evaluated against phantom freed/added capital. Rare trigger (DB write failure, not routine partial data), self-heals next 15-min cron tick (openRows re-fetched fresh), and mirrors an already-accepted tradeoff in commit.ts's own runningBook (mutated during planning, before executeSwingCommits' separate insert pass confirms each write) -- same repo, same pattern, not previously flagged as a bug there either. Not filing a fix: thin real-world impact vs. commit.ts's own established precedent for this shape. Revisit if a live repro ever surfaces (a roll that failed mid-batch with evidence a later same-pass candidate was mis-gated as a result).

open_experiments.summary: Investigated the WATCH lane's scanAsOf being stuck at 2026-09-22T16:00:10.502Z across 5+ checks spanning 16:47-19:10 UTC (watchCount:0 throughout). Logging this correction so a future session doesn't trust an unpaginated CloudWatch Logs query on a high-volume multi-stream Lambda log group again. (2) REAL EXPLANATION for most of the window: scan-cadence.ts's SWING_SCAN_PHASES defines 5 ET-windowed phases (PRE_OPEN/MIDDAY/POWER_HOUR/POST_CLOSE/OVERNIGHT) with GAPS between them where decideSwingScan returns run:false (cron still fires+200s, but no-ops, no re-persist) -- MIDDAY is 12:00-13:00 ET and claims ONCE per session day; the stuck scanAsOf (16:00:10Z UTC = 12:00:10 ET) is EXACTLY that single MIDDAY claim. The subsequent 13:00-15:00 ET gap (16:00-19:00 UTC, matching the swing-cadence-gap-recall-probe.mjs-documented gap) fully explains the flat scanAsOf through 18:30 UTC -- this is INTENDED, ALREADY-MEASURED-LOW-RISK cadence, not a bug. (3) ONE GENUINE RESIDUAL: POWER_HOUR (15:00-16:00 ET = 19:00-20:00 UTC) should have started a fresh scan at the 19:00 UTC firing, but BOTH the hit-cron Lambda logs AND the EventBridge rule-level Invocations metric show ZERO firing at/around 19:00 UTC (last confirmed: 18:36 metric bucket; next scheduled 19:30 UTC not yet due at time of writing). Rule confirmed still ENABLED, correct schedule, no FailedInvocations logged -- looks like a single transient EventBridge miss, not a config/outage issue. Single instance -- NOT escalating per the 3-instance threshold. NEXT CHECK: verify at/after 19:30 UTC whether scanAsOf finally advances (self-heals, matching every prior 30-min slot's reliability) or whether 19:30 ALSO misses (would make this 2 consecutive, worth escalating as a real EventBridge/cron gap). RESOLUTION (2026-09-22T19:31Z): re-checked the board -- scanAsOf advanced to 2026-09-22T19:03:10.556Z (watchCount still 0, a genuine zero-candidates scan, not a persistence failure). The scan landed ~3 min after the documented POWER_HOUR phase start (19:00 UTC), most likely CloudWatch Logs ingestion lag on my earlier metric/log check rather than a real EventBridge miss -- single transient instance, self-healed exactly as expected.
